tldr: When an order is created, create_order sends a confirmation email through the new notifications app. It implements the OpenSpec change add-order-confirmation, except the retries.
goal: Let customers know their order was registered, without putting email delivery in the orders app.

story.heading: create_order now sends the confirmation
story.body: After Order.place it calls send_order_confirmation, in the same transaction.

story.heading: notifications app added
story.body: It sends the email with send_mail. It depends on Order, in the allowed direction.

story.heading: The email goes out before the commit
story.body: send_order_confirmation runs inside transaction.atomic. If SMTP fails, the transaction rolls back.

story.heading: Order now requires a valid email
story.body: New email field with a migration. Order.place rejects emails without @.

story.heading: 2 of 3 scenarios met
story.body: The 'SMTP down' scenario is missing: there is no retry and the order is not created. Task 2.3 is still open.

components.summary: POST /orders/ passes the customer's email to create_order.
create_order takes the email and sends the confirmation.
Order stores and validates the email; new migration.
New app with send_order_confirmation on top of send_mail.

decisions.title: Send the email inside the transaction
decisions.why: It is the simplest option: no order is saved without a notice.
decisions.alternative: transaction.on_commit with a queued task and retries.

decisions.title: send_mail directly, with no interface of its own
decisions.why: Django already abstracts the email backend.
decisions.alternative: A Notifier interface in orders that notifications implements.

requirements.note: The 'SMTP down' scenario is not implemented: there is no retry and the order is not created.
